subject: Post-call: economic proofs & benchmarking requests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@parallax.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: economic proofs & benchmarking requests

Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Parallax is evaluating inference providers to replace a portion of your hyperscaler spend for production LLM features (multilingual summarization + chat).
- Primary evaluation criteria: per-1M token unit cost, 95th p99 latency at 1–2k rps, and cache/batching behavior for bursty RLHF-style traffic.
- You asked for reproducible proofs that show real-world delta vs the three hyperscaler endpoints you quoted.

What we propose (short list)
1) 1M-token synthetic run using your prompt mix (attached workbook has template). Report: per-1M token cost, end-to-end latency percentiles, GPU-time, and effective unit cost after 30%/50% cache hit.
2) Batching sensitivity matrix: run the same workload with batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and record per-token latency and throughput.
3) Prefix/KV-cache probe: simulate your 60% prefix reuse scenarios to show effective token savings and latency impact.

Requested from Parallax (what we need from you)
- A small prompt sample set (10–20 prompts representative of production) and a short traffic profile (95th percentile concurrency, % long vs short).
- Access window for a 2-hour bench run (we'll coordinate exact times).
- Any constraints for test infra (e.g., region, IP allowlisting).

Deliverables & timing
- Initial bench template + estimate: within 48 hours (attached workbook).
- Test execution and raw logs: within 5 business days of access.
- Consolidated readout with comparison vs hyperscaler claims: 2 business days after tests.

Commercial note
- We'll run everything on a sandbox account. If results look compelling, we can scope a short pilot (1–2 weeks, controlled traffic) and an exploratory pricing/commitment conversation.

Thanks again — I'll schedule the bench slot after you share the prompt set.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-econ-sample-1m.xlsx (template), hyperscaler-claim-log.txt (format for logging vendor claims)
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@parallax.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@parallax.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: economic proofs & benchmarking requests

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

1) Cost comparators: our team provided the three hyperscaler quotes (see attached reference earlier in the thread). For fairness, we need per-token math that includes their request-level overheads (e.g., network egress, model spin-up). Can you capture those in your comparison?

2) Cache assumptions: our production cache hit is variable; realistic windows are 40–65% depending on business hour. Please model both ends (40% and 65%).

3) Latency SLO: our customer SLA requires p95 < 400ms for short messages (<128 tokens) — can you show p95/p99 for both short and long classes?

4) Procurement will want a one-page artifact that summarizes the delta and highlights risk areas (model parity, failure modes).

We can provide the 25 sample prompts and a 24-hr traffic histogram by COB tomorrow. For bench window, next Thursday morning PT works well for us.

—Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Head of Platform | Parallax AI
jordan.hayes@parallax.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@parallax.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@parallax.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: economic proofs & benchmarking requests

Jordan — perfect, that gives us enough to finalize the bench plan. Quick answers inline: 

- Hyperscaler comparator accounting: yes — we'll add request-level overheads (egress/serialization) and show both token-only and fully-loaded unit costs. We'll call them: "raw token unit", "token + infra overhead", and "effective unit after cache."

- Cache modeling: we'll run the core runs at 40% and 65% hit rates. We'll also include a small sensitivity sweep (30–70%).

- Latency buckets: we'll split results into short (<128 tokens) and long (>=128 tokens) and report p50/p95/p99 plus 95th p99 tail with batching turned on/off.

Attached: redwood-econ-sample-1m.xlsx (fill in the prompt columns and traffic histogram). I also attached hyperscaler-claim-log.txt — please drop the quotes/metrics your team has and we will ingest them.

Proposed bench slot: Thursday 2027-04-22 08:00–10:00 PT. If that works, I’ll reserve capacity and share ephemeral keys and an allowlist IP for the run.

Next internal steps (for visibility)
- Marissa: please reserve a small dedicated slot on our infra for 4 GPUs and set logging level to include per-request KV-cache hits.
- Grace: please prep a short one-pager template for procurement (delta + risks + asking price).

Jordan — anything else we should add before Thursday?

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: redwood-econ-sample-1m.xlsx, hyperscaler-claim-log.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — Parallax bench prep (do not forward)

Folks — quick internal summary and asks after Jordan confirmed the prompt set and slot. Keeping this internal until we have the bench logs sanitized for procurement.

Context: Parallax wants a reproducible proof that our inference runtime yields lower effective per-token cost than their hyperscaler quotes when factoring cache and batching. They provided 25 prompts and a 24-hr concurrency histogram — sample looks aggressive at peak.

Immediate ops asks: 
- Reserve 4x A100-equivalent machines for Thu 08:00–10:00 PT. Ensure we enable KV prefix cache metrics and per-request GPU-time reporting.
- Run the 1M-token synthetic as: 1) raw streaming no-batch, 2) batching at [4,8,16], 3) cache-sim at 40% and 65% reuse. Log format: timestamp, prompt-id, model-variant, request-latency-ms, tokens-generated, cache-hit-boolean, gpu-ms.

Analysis plan: Marissa — you will produce the per-1M token report and a short 1pg delta narrative. Grace — draft procurement one-pager and recommended pilot pricing (3 options: trial free, pilot discount, 12-month commit).

Risks to note in the readout (we will surface): model-quality parity on long-form, cold-start variance for multi-region traffic, and egress/network accounting alignment.

I'll circulate the final bench link and HubSpot note after the run.

Ben
